sb_prompt: DISCUSS THE WEATHER.   WHAT HAS IT BEEN LIKE IN YOUR AREA?   HAS IT BEEN TYPICAL FOR THIS TIME OF YEAR?  COMPARE IT WITH THE OTHER CALLER'S WEATHER.
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Is this the right number to speak with someone about the local weather conditions?
ParticipantB: Yes, I can certainly discuss the weather here. What seems to be the issue?
ParticipantA: I'm actually just curious. I'm currently in the Midwest, and it's been incredibly cold here.
ParticipantB: Oh, really? That's surprising. It has been unusually warm here in the South recently.
ParticipantA: Really? I thought that time of year usually brought us freezing temperatures. What has it been like in your area?
ParticipantB: Well, we've had highs in the mid-70s for the last three days. It feels like late spring or early summer right now.
ParticipantA: That is a stark contrast. In my region, we just got hit by a nor'easter that dropped us to ten degrees.
ParticipantB: Ten degrees? That must be brutal. For us, the temps are usually in the 50s or low 60s right now.
ParticipantA: It certainly isn't typical for this time of year here. We are expecting snow tomorrow.
ParticipantB: That sounds harsh. Have you seen any snow yet?
ParticipantA: Actually, yes. There was an inch of dusting on the ground this morning, but it melted by noon.
ParticipantB: That's strange. We haven't had a single flake. The ground is still brown and dry.
ParticipantA: It feels very dry here too, though the humidity is much higher than you'd expect in December.
ParticipantB: The humidity is the main thing for us. It makes the heat feel oppressive, almost like July.
ParticipantA: I can imagine. We are getting used to the dry, crisp winter air, but the sudden drop was shocking.
ParticipantB: I suppose it is a bit of a shock. I checked the forecast, and they say we might cool down slightly tomorrow.
ParticipantA: That would be a relief. Do you think it will get back to normal winter weather soon?
ParticipantB: Probably not for another week or so. It looks like a warm front is staying put.
ParticipantA: That is unfortunate. It makes it hard to imagine proper winter clothing for everyone down there.
ParticipantB: It's definitely disorienting. People are complaining about mosquitoes appearing unexpectedly.
ParticipantA: That is wild. I was just buying thermal socks. I hope you don't have to deal with bugs.
ParticipantB: I don't know. Maybe the bugs will stay hidden in the shade, but it feels wrong.
ParticipantA: I've been telling my neighbors to just ignore the forecast models and expect summer.
ParticipantB: Sounds like we are swapping stories about our opposite experiences quite well.
ParticipantA: Yes, it's fascinating to compare our two completely different worlds at the same time.
ParticipantB: Exactly. It really highlights how variable the climate can be across the country.
ParticipantA: I'm glad I could get some insight from you. It makes my cold snap feel less isolated.
ParticipantB: I'm glad too. It makes my heat wave feel a little more unique.
ParticipantA: Have you experienced anything like this warm streak before in your history?
ParticipantB: Not really. We usually have a few days of 60-degree weather, but not sustained 70s.
ParticipantA: That seems to be the new normal for this region lately. Our winters are getting milder.
ParticipantB: It seems our summers are getting longer and our winters shorter.
ParticipantA: It certainly makes packing for trips difficult when you don't know what to expect.
ParticipantB: Exactly. I bought a light jacket, and now I'm wondering if I need a heavy coat after all.
ParticipantA: Just stay flexible. We are wrapping up our heavy coats at home anyway.
ParticipantB: Good advice. It saves money on unnecessary purchases.
ParticipantA: I think that's about all I wanted to ask regarding the weather patterns.
ParticipantB: Me too. It has been a very interesting exchange comparing our zones.
ParticipantA: Thank you for chatting with me about your area's conditions.
ParticipantB: You are welcome. Take care out there in the cold.
ParticipantA: You too. Stay safe.
ParticipantB: Goodbye!
ParticipantA: Goodbye!
